report:
The r5 head exists. Diffing it against this head.

NO DEFECTS

I found no defect at `5f8fe266` that the author must fix before merge. I diffed this head against the round-five head (`5e3f22a3`, still present under `heads/`) and replayed the earlier probes that still apply, all at this head.

## NOT A DEFECT

**Earlier findings and whether each is closed at this head**

| Earlier finding | At this head | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Claude F1: the Vertex OAuth token request was counted as a model request | **Closed** | `createVertexAuthenticatedFetch` and `streamGoogleVertex` now fetch the token through `uncountedFetchOf(...)`. I replayed `probe-vertex.test.ts` unchanged (`GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=p GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=us-east5`): two URLs (token, then `:streamRawPredict`), and `stopReason: stop providerReplays: 0`. Round five reported `1`. |
| Claude F2: a single held call can put 12 identical bodies on one model | Unchanged, by design | Still limited to one such call per recovery by `#connectionHoldClosed`. The round-five reviewer recorded it as out of scope, and I agree. |
| Claude F3: a hold could be charged without being taken | **Closed** | `#connectionHoldsSpent++` now runs only inside `if (chainConsultable && connectionHold)`, so a hold is spent only where it replaces a chain consult. |
| Claude F4: capacity evidence that exists only as glued digits is erased | Residual, synthetic | `connection reset by peer (upstream-529)` is still classified `Connection`, the same as round five. `GLUED_NUMBER_PATTERN` did not change. |
| Astra: the authentication resend reported zero replays | **Closed** | I replayed `auth-replay.test.ts` unchanged. Direct `streamSimple`: 2 requests, the error reports `replays: 1` (round five: `0`). Session mode: 2 primary requests, then `retry_fallback_applied` to `gpt-4o`. Round five sent six primary requests and reported zero three times. This comes from the per-request counter: `providerReplaysFrom` no longer takes `start`, and `withWireCount` / `wireAttemptsOf(options.fetch)` are shared across re-entries. |
| Astra: `abortRetry()` racing a reported replay reopened the hold | **Closed** | I replayed `life-reset-race.test.ts` unchanged. Counts are now Sonnet 12, Opus 1, Haiku 1, gpt-4o 1; round five was 12/1/12/1. `abortRetry()` now calls `#releaseRetry()` and keeps the hold state. A pending wait still ends through `#endCancelledRetry` → `resolveRetry()`, and `resetForNewPrompt()` clears the state. |
| Astra: timing values were read as status or capacity evidence | **Closed** | I replayed `classifier-extra.ts`. Every `retry-after-ms=N`, `elapsed_ms=N`, glued-identifier and URL variant (N = 399 to 8000) is now `connection:true, retry:true`. The "saved under terminal" and "named under terminal" rows are identical to the main-branch log, so they predate this change. |
| Astra: the held-sleep boundary was inclusive | **Closed** | The check is now `sameModelDelayMs === 0 \|\| sameModelDelayMs < heldWindowMs`, so a hint exactly at the window consults the chain. I did not rerun the 16-second timing probe. |
| Astra: credential rotation after the hold closed; native compression accounting | Unchanged, correct | No change touches these paths. The shared counter still counts the uncompressed resend; `provider-replays.test.ts` passes. |

**Suspicions I checked and ruled out**

- **The counter now covers the whole request rather than each call.** Any request sent through the same counted fetch before the provider runs would now count as an attempt. I looked for such requests in `stream.ts`, `anthropic.ts`, `openai-codex-responses.ts` and `cursor.ts`: the only one is the Vertex token, which is now uncounted. A `prepareRequest` wrapper that does not pass the counter on makes the count unknown (`undefined`), which suppresses holds rather than inventing them. The connection prewarm builds its own transport fetch, and the main agent loop passes no `fetch`.
- **The direct `streamAnthropic` default transport.** With no `fetch` given, `wireCountedFetch` counts over the global `fetch`. The main branch also fell back to the global `fetch` (`args.fetch ?? fetch` in `buildAnthropicClientOptions`), so nothing regressed.
- **The new field-number stripping (`FIELD_NUMBER_PATTERN`) on realistic wording.** These all keep their status: `status: 503`, `status=401`, `http_status=503`, `upstream_status=529`, `HTTP 503`, `Error: 401` and Cloudflare/Go-style `code: …`. Fields outside the allow-list (`error_code=529`, `errorCode=401`, `"error_code": 429`, `API-Error: 401`) do lose their number and can classify as `Connection`. I found no provider that emits these shapes, so I am not asserting it as a defect. It is the same family as F4.
- **Bare status numbers removed before `TRANSIENT_TRANSPORT_PATTERN` runs.** The `auth-gateway 503:` arm still matches through the second test, which reads `withoutMetadataNumbers`. Removing a number does not join wording into a new match (`service 503 unavailable` leaves a double space, which `.?` does not span).
- **The hold now spends only where the chain is consultable.** When there is no chain, a candidate keeps `heldRetryIndex = 1`, so attempt 2 gets full jitter in [0, 500) ms instead of [0, 1000) ms. This is a tuning difference, not a correctness bug.
- **The floor and unknown-count logic in `withReplaySafeStreamRetry`.** With one shared counter the reports only rise, so the floor guard only strips a report that is impossible. Moving the retry-counter increments to after the wait does not change behaviour: a failed wait returns either way.

**Focused tests at this head:**
- `agent-session-wire-retry-requests.test.ts`: 11 pass.
- `provider-replays.test.ts`, `empty-completion-retry.test.ts` and `connection-failure-classification.test.ts`: 377 pass, 0 fail.

The repository-wide typecheck and suite were not available in this window.
